Q: How to configure vmlens-maven-plugin to fail on deadlock in CI/CD? A:

What do you mean by failing on deadlock?

Parallel programming is not based on failing deadlocks. The only approach is to avoid deadlocks in principle, no matter what happens. Hanging indefinitely is a correct behavior during the execution of the incorrect application. Moreover, the most dangerous behavior is not hanging for a long time. Isn't it obvious why?

Now, there are systems for deadlock detection. They have limited capacity. In particular, I tested some of them and found that none of them can detect the well-known dining philosophers problem deadlock. As far as I know, it is theoretically proven that automatic deadlock detection for all possible cases is undecidable.

Q: Flask redirect causes session details not modified A:

For mutable structures within the session memory, changes are not applied automatically. For this purpose, there is the attribute modified, to which a boolean value of True can be manually assigned. This ensures that the changes are applied.

session.modified = True

Q: Can't get chrome to trust my self signed ssl certificate A:

What finally worked for me was to run in administrator powershell terminal:

Import-Certificate -FilePath "path\my\root-ca.crt" -CertStoreLocation "Cert:\LocalMachine\Root"

Afterwards, chrome would not complain about my selfhosted page being unsecure.

Before, I mistakenly installed it as an "Intermediate CA" instead of a "Trusted Root CA". I did that by opening the crt-file via explorer and importing via the windows GUI, yet that approach was a dead end.

Further context for SEO:

I wanted to get docker pull, yet attempts to pull from my selfhosted gitlab failed due to security issues, due to my https connection being selfsigned.

My problem also affected curl:

PowerShell 7.6.0
(sentinel) PS C:\Users\Philipp\PycharmProjects\sentinel> curl -v https://gitlab.local
* Host gitlab.local:443 was resolved.
* IPv6: (none)
* IPv4: 10.0.10.105
*   Trying 10.0.10.105:443...
* schannel: disabled automatic use of client certificate
* ALPN: curl offers http/1.1
* schannel: SEC_E_UNTRUSTED_ROOT (0x80090325) - The certificate chain was issued by an authority that is not trusted.
* closing connection #0
curl: (60) schannel: SEC_E_UNTRUSTED_ROOT (0x80090325) - The certificate chain was issued by an authority that is not trusted.
More details here: https://curl.se/docs/sslcerts.html

curl failed to verify the legitimacy of the server and therefore could not
establish a secure connection to it. To learn more about this situation and
how to fix it, please visit the webpage mentioned above.

curl is still a bit wonky and if I do curl -v https://gitlab.local, it fails via:

CRYPT_E_NO_REVOCATION_CHECK (0x80092012)

yet

curl -v --ssl-no-revoke https://gitlab.local

works.

What mattered to me most now is that after trusting my root certificate, I finally could run docker pull; as this was the actual issue I tried to solve: pulling images from a selfhosted gitlab instance.

I did add in my docker for windows config "insecure-registries though before, not sure if this is required:

{
  "builder": {
    "gc": {
      "defaultKeepStorage": "20GB",
      "enabled": true
    }
  },
  "experimental": false,
  "insecure-registries": [
    "gitlab.local",
    "registry.local"
  ]
}
